summary.text: Zach Lahn is a farmer and businessman who won the Republican nomination for Iowa governor in an upset. He runs an 'Iowa First' campaign that opposes abortion and high taxes and defends gun rights and school vouchers. He co-founded a private school in Wichita, Kansas, and registered to vote in Iowa in October 2024.

paragraphs.text: Lahn grew up near Sioux City, Iowa, and graduated from the University of Colorado Boulder.
He worked for Montana and Colorado congressmen and served as Montana director of Americans for Prosperity.
In 2018 he co-founded Wonder, a private pre-K to 12 school that opened in Wichita, Kansas.
Kansas voter records show he voted in Kansas in 2018, 2020 and 2022, and he registered to vote in Iowa on October 17, 2024.

He bought a farm in Belle Plaine, Iowa, that relatives previously owned, describes himself as a sixth-generation farmer, and founded Homeplace Ventures, an Iowa-based company focused on agriculture, real estate and technology investments.
Lahn launched his campaign for governor in November 2025.
He won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary over Rep. Randy Feenstra, who had been endorsed by President Donald Trump, and faces Democrat Rob Sand in November.
